answer.rationale: The finance mandate of 18% spend reduction is non-negotiable and immediate. memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to the low-cost vendor has already proven successful (quick onboarding, accurate invoicing, sharp unit cost reduction). The incumbent's most recent lever—multi-year commitments (memory_c6)—is not available within the 14-day window. Renegotiation (memory_c4) alone is unlikely to meet an 18% target without multi-year lock-in. The low-cost vendor's quote already meets the mandate, eliminating the need for second-sourcing complexity or deferral. However, the assembly line running at 94% capacity creates material delivery risk: any disruption in the switch could force expedite penalties or brief volume shortfall. A standard_experiment scale (parallel orders during transition, verified invoicing and delivery SLAs before full cutover) mitigates this risk while meeting the deadline. The primary risk is transition timing and vendor reliability under volume—both addressable through staged implementation rather than full rollout on day one.
